title: Shimon the Modest
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman says he was a priest who also served in the Temple. At the beginning of Tosefta Kelim, Bava Kamma, chapter 1, he tells Rabbi Eliezer: “I entered between the porch and altar without washing my hands and feet.” Eliezer asks him: “Who is more beloved—you or the High Priest?” Shimon remains silent. Eliezer asks: “Are you ashamed to say that the High Priest’s dog is more beloved than you?” Shimon replies: “My teacher, did you say that?” Eliezer answers: “By the Temple service! Even a High Priest’s skull is split with logs. What could you have done? The baal ha-pol did not find you.”

notes.text: The final בעל הפול remains unexplained here; it is not translated as an official in charge of beans. “By the Temple service!” is an oath. The Tosefta request was unavailable, so the final wording remains a source question.

The saved whole Machon Mamre Tosefta Kelim Kamma1:6 contains the dialogue and full Rabbi Eliezer, including the comparison of Shimon with the High Priest, the dog retort and בעל הפול. It omits the supplied העבודה oath; the oath is preserved as By the Temple service rather than removed to match this edition. Temple guard/inspector is a dictionary/Rashash search-snippet lead, not a full commentary inspection, so baal ha-pol remains unresolved rather than official over beans. Priest and Temple-service status are Hyman’s characterization. The paragraph is whole; it is not a whole-chapter or legal adjudication.

Tosefta Kelim Kamma 1:6 preserves the dialogue and the term baal ha-pol. Hyman uses the oath “By the Temple service,” as does the quotation in Tosafot on Sanhedrin 83a. The latter explains baal ha-pol as the Temple Mount officer who inspected the premises and connects the term with the verb in ein polin. Saul Lieberman instead connects the name with pol, “bean,” comparing other nicknames. The two interpretations leave the title itself visible in the translation.
